about.title: About Debt Payoff Calculator
about.description: The Debt Payoff Calculator helps you create an effective strategy to eliminate your debts faster and save money on interest payments. This comprehensive tool analyzes your current debts, calculates payoff timelines, and compares different repayment strategies including debt snowball and debt avalanche methods. Whether you're dealing with credit card debt, student loans, or multiple debts, this calculator provides personalized recommendations to accelerate your path to financial freedom.

faq.q: What's the difference between debt snowball and debt avalanche?
faq.a: Debt snowball focuses on paying off the smallest balance first for psychological motivation, while debt avalanche targets the highest interest rate first to save more money. Avalanche saves more on interest, but snowball provides quicker wins.

faq.q: How much extra should I pay toward my debts?
faq.a: Pay as much extra as your budget allows after covering essential expenses and emergency savings. Even an extra $25-50 per month can significantly reduce payoff time and interest costs.

faq.q: Should I pay off debt or save money first?
faq.a: Build a small emergency fund ($500-1000) first, then focus on high-interest debt. Once debt is paid off, build a full 3-6 month emergency fund while continuing to save and invest.

faq.q: Is debt consolidation a good option?
faq.a: Debt consolidation can be beneficial if you qualify for a lower interest rate than your current debts. However, it requires discipline to avoid accumulating new debt on the paid-off accounts.
